instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice and get it cooking first. The fish and the sauce take about 20 minutes once you start.
Pat the 1 1/2 lb fish completely dry with paper towels and cut it into 4 pieces. Cut 2 or 3 shallow slashes across the top of each piece and sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt over both sides.

Peel the 8 garlic cloves. Cut the stems off the 2 Fresno chilies and scrape out the seeds. Pound the garlic and chilies together in a mortar until they're broken up but still rough, or chop them together on the board until they're fine.

In a small bowl, stir together 2 tbsp tamarind concentrate, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce and 1/4 cup water. Slice the 4 Thai chilies into a little dish for the table, and pick a good handful of cilantro leaves.

Pour the 1 1/2 cups oil into a large skillet and heat it over medium high for about 4 minutes. Meanwhile, spread the 1/3 cup cornstarch on a plate and press each piece of fish into it on every side. Shake off the extra.

Drop a pinch of cornstarch into the oil. If it sizzles right away, it's ready. Lay in half the fish, skin side down if it has skin, laying each piece away from you. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.
Fry the fish without moving it for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and crisp.

Flip the pieces and cook the other side for about 3 minutes, until it's golden too. The fish is done when it flakes easily at the thickest part. Transfer it to a rack or a paper towel lined plate, then fry the second half the same way.
Carefully spoon the hot oil out of the pan into a heatproof bowl, leaving about 2 tbsp behind. Turn the heat down to medium low.
Add the garlic and chili paste and stir it for about 1 minute, until it smells fragrant and the garlic turns pale gold. Keep it moving. Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter.
Pour in the tamarind mixture. Let it bubble, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sugar melts and the sauce turns glossy and about as thick as maple syrup. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.
Set the fish on a platter, spoon the hot sauce over it right before it goes to the table and scatter the cilantro leaves on top. Serve with the jasmine rice and the sliced Thai chilies on the side.
method_notes: All three fry the fish until crisp, then fry pounded garlic and chilies in a little of the oil and simmer them with tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce into a sweet, sour and hot sauce that goes over the fish at the end, with cilantro and jasmine rice. Hungry in Thailand and Real Thai Recipes fry a whole scored fish (Hungry in Thailand says thick white fillets work too) and Hungry in Thailand dusts it in cornstarch, while ImportFood adds a short oven crisp. This one uses fillets for a weeknight, keeps the sauce mild with seeded Fresno chilies standing in for long red chilies, puts the Thai chilies on the side, and uses brown sugar for palm sugar. ImportFood's 3 is a review count, not a rating count; no version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Thai) has only a chilli lime fish, a different dish, so the version with the most ratings leads.
